extracted.intended_audience: instrument-makers, natural philosophers, mirror-makers, and painters interested in practical optics
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidelines and explanatory principles for making, arranging, and using mirrors, prisms, and reflective surfaces (including parabolic/spherical/planar reflectors) and for observing colours and images. Includes geometric construction rules, material recommendations, and observational/positioning criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Igniting fire with concave/parabolic specula
rubrics_metrics.description: Hec autem ab Archimede plané demonstrata sunt ... primus, vt omnes radij in centrum speculi incidant & colligantur in uno puncto per reflexionem; qui fit, vt dicitur, cum cauo speculo sphaerico. Secundus est, vt omnes equidistantes colligantur ... qui etiam fit parabole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concave surface (spherical in parts, but parabola is best) to gather solar rays to a single point to ignite; Archimedes' method and Antonio Gogauas' examples cited. Construct via sections of spheres/cones/parabolas: make the surface equidistant from the axis (parabole) so that reflected rays meet in a point. Practical notes include making large portions of sphere/cone/parabola (portiones maximarum spherarum, aut conorum maximorum), backing glass with lead (specula ... superasperfo plumbo) and using well-tempered iron (chalybe) for frame; given worked examples for long distances (e.g. loci ad comburendum mille passibus distantem) with proportional construction steps (divide diameters, form cones, derive parabola by geometric sections) to focus at desired range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinants of the strength (robor) of reflected rays
rubrics_metrics.description: Causa autem roboris radiorum per accidés dicuntur, magnitudo & propinquitas lucidi & quod radius ille ex centro lucidi proficiscatur: tum sinceritas medij & radiorum ipsorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflected intensity depends on: size of the luminous surface (larger lucidi), proximity of the mirror to the luminous source and to the target, whether the reflected ray proceeds from the luminous object's center, and the clearness/purity of the medium and rays. Thus rays reflected near perpendicular and near the mirror's center are stronger; nearer mirrors yield greater perceived force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpendicular incidence increases reflected power
rubrics_metrics.description: Enim reflectitur a perpendiculo in seipsum multiplicatur ... proximissimae partibus maior est vis, quoniam radius radio proxime est.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a ray reflects from a surface near perpendicular to itself (i.e., incident near the normal), the resulting reflected force (heat/robor) is effectively multiplied — nearer-to-perpendicular reflections and rays nearer the mirror's center produce larger heating effects. Use perpendicular or near-perpendicular geometry to maximize thermal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polished surfaces give image but little heat
rubrics_metrics.description: Quinta est; cum a corpore non polito reflectuntur radij, ad visum inutiles; non ad calorem: nam & hi perpendiculares ... reflexio imaginem haud reddunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surfaces that reflect rays purely to produce clear images (polished bodies) are effective for vision but not for producing warmth/ignition; polished reflections form images without delivering the concentrated caloric effect produced by certain concave/rough reflections used for heating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and arrangement of two mirrors to see hidden or distant objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculum sublimi immobile a directo loci suspendes latentis, ita ut speculi facies plano tuo perpendiculares immineat: speculi autem mobilis facies longitudinem loco quem desideras oppositam habeat ... circumvoluto mobili speculo, donec quale angulum faciat; quod oculus tibi declarabit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspend an immobile mirror with its face perpendicular toward the hidden locus; use a mobile mirror (or a wrapped mobile speculum) that you rotate until the desired angle shows the hidden place. The mobile mirror's face should be opposite the line of sight to the desired location. Tripod support recommended; precise angular control and perpendicularity are crucial for correct viewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-image generation by planar mirrors (angles and placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sunt & specula quae multas facies ostendunt ... Si specula duo continentia ... in una superficie plana existens collocaveris, vt altero ad te accedentre; reliquum abiccedat, ... videbis imaginem tuam accedente in alterum et in reliquo retrocedentem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple faces/images are produced by arranging planar mirrors at particular relative angles; equal-angle incidence/reflection rules govern multiplicity and order of images. Using two or more planar mirrors (inclined appropriately) yields double, triple, or more images; increasing mirror size and correct relative positioning increases visibility and quality of repeated images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric construction procedure for a parabolic reflector
rubrics_metrics.description: Sit locus qui comburi debet mille passibus distans. Facio 5 x passuum mille cui reacta ... facio conum, & describetur circulus ... duco igitur a vertice coni rectam ad extremitatem unius diametri basi ... inde assumte partes ex gypsio maiorè latitudine ... efficièsque parabolen ... aptabis, efficiésque parabolen quae à tergo superasperfo plumbo radios omnes e Sole quiedistant qui omnium sunt robustissimi in punctum x ... comburentque statim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To make a parabola for burning distant objects, derive the parabola from a cone section: describe circles, divide diameters at right angles, draw the axis from the cone vertex, take appropriate transverse sections and build the parabola frame of iron/lead-backed glass or polished metal; use gypsum/moulds to form the curved surface, and place a lead backing to strengthen the reflector. The text gives proportional steps (dividing diameters, erecting oblique lines, selecting lateral segments) to produce a parabola that focuses solar rays to a fixed point at the intended distance (worked example for 1000 paces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer parabola (or suitable spherical sections) over simple circles for remote burning
rubrics_metrics.description: Parabole praecedit coflagratio potentior est. Ea autem sic fit. Sit locus qui comburi debet mille passibus distans ... ex parabole sumpta; res autem sic se habet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A parabolic reflector is the most effective shape for concentrating parallel solar rays from a distance; large spherical/circular portions may also work but with less efficiency. For distant targets prefer a parabola (or appropriately large spherical/conic portions) to gather rays in one focal point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mirror material, backing and framing recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Hec autem ab Archimede plané demonstrata sunt ... inde assumte partes ex chalybe optimo, ne flectantur, fieri oportet; assumpta tantum parte ... huic moli vitrum candens aptabis, efficiésque parabolen quae à tergo superasperfo plumbo ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use good iron (chalybe) for frames/strips to avoid flexing, form rigid ribs for the curved surface; fit heated glass to the frame and back it with lead (plumbeo) for support. Polished metals and well-tempered iron will maintain shape; avoid materials that bend under weight or heat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image size and apparent distance depend on mirror size and relative placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Quod si profundum obsucrad ut uterum ... medium ... colloca ... videbis cuncta ut in luce clara ... annulus ex aduetrio speculo collocaveris annulus vero & ipse speculi fit, velut inclusus Sapphiro, videbis in speculo imagine annuli in cuius gemma imago tua apparebit; hoc autem ex multiplici reflexione continget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger mirrors, rings, or inserted objects change apparent size and distance of images; placing objects (rings, gems) near or on the mirror produces multiplicative/reflected images. Positioning between viewer and object alters apparent magnification; deeper/profound settings and multiple reflections yield richer illusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using prisms and faceted crystal (prisma) to multiply images and produce colours
rubrics_metrics.description: Crystal prismam ... multis speculorum vites habet, ut quod multa forman referat, tum etiam auerfas capitibus & pedibus supra ... colores maxime ... pulcherrimos & inimitabiles apparebunt ... verum oculis applicatum; tum maxime ubi arbores sint & prata; pulchritudinem caelestem refert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A crystal prism with faceting produces many mirror-like faces and splendid, varied colours, especially when oriented relative to the sun and natural scenery. Use pure crystal (large, clear crystal) and appropriate alignment with light to produce vivid and varied chromatic effects; prisms can act as many small specula to display colours and multiply forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour arrangement and painting guidance (avoid overuse of white)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceterum vt ad picturam revertar, nec obiter colores sunt disponendi, sed inter claros obstur i & inter obscuros clari se debent habere; decorum & ornamentum picturae adducunt. Ergo rubeus inter caeruleum & viridem; candidus inter cines reum & croceum interponendus erit. Sed cauendum est; ne candidus multum in picturis utaris.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange colours considering relations of light/dark and neighbour colours: place red between blue and green, place white judiciously between certain tones, and avoid excessive use of white which can spoil splendour and decorum. Balance of clear and obscure tones is essential for ornament and the proper effect of paintings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour origins: material, light, and medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Generantur colores ex tribus: primum quidem subiecta materia: inde luce, seu potius lumine quod ei miscetur, & medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colours arise from three causes: the subject-matter (material), the light (or luminous source mixing with it), and the medium through which the object is viewed. Therefore, to change perceived colour you can act on material, illumination, or intervening medium (e.g., crystal, glass, atmosphere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation of planar mirrors relative to the sun and Earth (daily/seasonal declination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quomodo igitur à planis plana speculis perpendicularis fiet reflexio? ... produc ta ex centro Solis ad superficiem speculi recti transfit ... pro tempore anni dicitur declinatio ... Ficque perpetuo anno radios perpendiculares excipiet, vt ante tempus holera & fructus habere possis reddatur ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A planar surface will reflect perpendicular solar rays only when its normal is aimed at the Sun's centre for the given declination/day; to receive perpendicular rays throughout the year, align/erect surfaces according to the Sun's declination arcs (divide the circle into appropriate arcs corresponding to the Sun's daily/seasonal path). Use these alignments to direct winter sunlight perpendicular to interior spaces for heating/illumination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of medium (air vs water) and binocular occlusion on perceived duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Quod si homines volantes videre in speculo libeat ... Sunt & qui specula finxerunt tot facies ... Etiam de aquas falsas imagines referam, scilicet quomodo res una videri possint ... Cum igitur obliquantur oculi, vt nervi flectuntur & deorsum deprimantur, una res duo videbitur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Viewing through different media (air vs water) or when the eyes are occluded/obliqued produces double images; the medium and angle of incidence can split perceived objects into two even when they are single. For correct single perception, maintain proper alignment and be aware that water, glass, and relative occlusion produce duplicates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using veils, curtains and controlled occlusion to compose painted/seen form
rubrics_metrics.description: Si umbra igitur umbroso corpus. Adeo enim sensus aufuereus iudicio ... Altera est, ut consideres quae pars corporis videatur ... inde umbra ad lumen quod ante te finges ad latitudinem dimidii reici collocabis ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To render form convincingly (in painting or perception) place shadows and occluding veils to emulate the way the eye judges parts of bodies; consider which surface parts are visible and which are latent, place shadow relative to light as if at half the body's breadth to create convincing depth. Managing occlusion and shadow is part of composing believable images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clock-face and rotating-mirror constructions to produce sequenced faces (mechanical multiplicity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inde partes omnes in ... ut tempora translationum fiant qualia ... ut sint tres rotae ... ita fiet ut cum post primi tetramorphim facta, inde tertia detegatur, atque in singulis facies singule ut pro horarum numero ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By subdividing reflective surfaces and mounting rotating elements (wheels/rotas/tetramorphis), one can produce sequences of faces/images corresponding to hour divisions or other periodic displays. Use unequal wheel radii and off-center mounting to change apparent motion speed and produce moving faces for horological or theatrical displays.
